summary: Henry Creswicke Rawlinson was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Great Ealing School and Middlesex University, later serving with the East India Company, Foreign Office, and Royal Asiatic Society as director and president.

Henry George Keene worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Fort William College and Sidney Sussex College, served with the East India Company, and was Professor of Arabic, Persian, and Hindústání Literature at East India Company College.

Henry Hamilton Hadley specialized in religious studies and linguistics. Educated at Yale College, Yale Divinity School, Union Theological Seminary, and Andover Theological Seminary, he held posts as professor of Hebrew at Yale and professor of Hebrew at Union Theological Seminary.

Henry Herbert Dodwell was a historian and Indologist educated at Lord Williams's School and St John's College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Education Service (1908–1922) and was Professor of History and Culture of the British Dominions in Asia at SOAS.
Henry Martyn was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Truro Cathedral School, St John's College, and under John Borthwick Gilchrist.
Henry Miers Elliot worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Winchester College, he served as a civil servant for the East India Company from circa 1826 to 1853.

Henry Pitts Forster was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He served in the East India Company's Bengal service and Bengal Civil Service from 1783 to 1815, and was Master of the Calcutta Mint from 1803 to 1804.
Henry Sullivan Jarrett worked in history and archaeology. He served as Secretary and Member of the Board of Examiners in Calcutta from circa 1870 to 1896, succeeding Heinrich Blochmann.

Indologist Henry Thomas Colebrooke studied under Citrapati. He served with the East India Company, held a professorship of Sanskrit at Fort William College, sat on the Supreme Council of Bengal, and was president of the Royal Asiatic Society and Royal Astronomical Society.

Herbert Cushing Tolman worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Yale, Peabody College, University of Nashville, Hobart College, and University of Louisville, he held posts at Yale, Wisconsin-Madison, UNC Chapel Hill, and Vanderbilt University.

Herbert Franke studied sinology and Central Asian studies at Bonn, Berlin, and Cologne under Erich Haenisch and Erich Hauer. He held posts at the University of Cologne, University of Munich, and served as president of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Herbert Hope Risley was an Indologist and historian who studied at Winchester College (circa 1863–1869) and New College (circa 1869–1873).

Herbert Härtel worked in Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg and Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt. He served at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, directed the Museum of Asian Art, and held professorships at Humboldt and Free universities.

Herbert Niel Randle worked in Indology and philosophy. He was professor of philosophy at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (circa 1910–1927) and served as Librarian at the India Office and India Office Records (1927–1949).

Herbert V. Guenther studied Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies at Munich and Vienna under Wilhelm Geiger and Walther Wüst, alongside traditional teachers. He held posts at Vienna, Lucknow, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and headed Far Eastern Studies at the University of Saskatchewan.

Herbert Weir Smyth was a scholar in linguistics and classics. He studied at Swarthmore, Harvard, Leipzig, and Göttingen under Hermann Sauppe, later holding posts at Williams College, Johns Hopkins, Bryn Mawr College, and Harvard University.
Herbert Zachert was a scholar of Japanology who studied under Karl Florenz. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1941–1945) and the University of Bonn (circa 1960–1976).

Herman Kellgren worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Eugène Burnouf, Philippe-Édouard Foucaux, and Hermann Brockhaus, and held a post at the University of Helsinki from circa 1849 to 1856.

Hermann Beckh was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kiel University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the Kiel Institute for the World Economy, Berlin State Library, and Humboldt University of Berlin.
Hermann Berger was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Helmut Hoffmann. He held a post at Heidelberg University from circa 1964 to 1992.
